t: A low-power chip with a built-in LoRa radio for long-range sensors.
steps: Buy a Seeed Wio-E5 Dev Kit for about 27 US dollars or an Olimex LoRa-STM32WL-DevKit.
Check that the radio band matches your country, such as 868 MHz in Europe or 915 MHz in North America.
Attach the antenna before you power the board.
Try the factory AT command firmware first from a serial terminal app.
Install the free Arduino IDE and add the stm32duino board package.
Add the STM32LoRaWAN library and open its basic send example.
Register your node on a LoRaWAN network and watch the first message arrive.
meta: Wild Open. From $5.99. A few stores.
